text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The present level of taxation harms the interests of the small and medium-sized private companies, the paper says.
- Tax evasion is on the rise, the paper said.
- Italy's New Holland farm equipment maker decided to continue its operation in Romania following the new amendments brought to the law on foreign investment.
- Total direct foreign investments in post-communist Romania exceed 2.4 billion.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Sales of Romania's 1997 grain crop might be affected by the inefficient commodities exchange system, the paper said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Communications Ministry plans to raise telephone tariffs starting September 1.
- The coalmine Leorda, in northeastern Romania, will be closed down due to poor economic performance, the paper said.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Transport Ministry got a $185 million credit from Japan for projects in the infrastructure.
- The government will allocate 140 billion lei to support youth who graduate high-schools and universities.
- Romania will export four-wheel drive vehicles made by ARO Cimpulung to the United States, the paper said.
- Tarom SA state airline will cut 1,250 jobs, the paper quotes Transport Minister Traian Basescu as saying.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Some eight tonnes of crude oil polluted a field near Ploiesti when thieves punctured an oil pipeline to steal petrol, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The paper publishes a list of persons who acted as illegal advisers to the former leftist government and who still use their old credentials to get favours.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Romania will find itself into a "security deficit" after the NATO summit in Madrid, where the Balkan country will not be invited to join NATO in its first enlargement, the paper quotes Chief of Staff General Constantin Degeratu, as saying.
- Police investigate a mass grave in the Insula Mare a Brailei, believed to contain the remains of former political prisoners jailed by the former communist authorities in the 1950s.
- A conference of the opposition Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR) called for the resignation of the centrist government, the paper said.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
